messages:
sylvie: Thinking out loud — proposal to add a lightweight RBAC "frontier" proxy in the Console path. Idea: console -> frontier (authz) -> query service. Frontier returns pre-filtered ids + cache keys so panels can MTU few small queries instead of full fanout.

mike: curious — how is this different from authz pushdown we already talked about for query layer?

sylvie: pushdown lives in query service and is great for full coverage, but it breaks panel-level caching and adds variable work per request. Frontier keeps RBAC decisions deterministic & cacheable at panel-bounds.

nina: can we get numbers? rough perf delta and complexity tradeoffs?

sylvie: from local perf runs (toy data): panel call without frontier: p95=360ms, CPU spikes on query nodes due to many tenants. With frontier (pre-filter ids + cached policy): p95=280ms, median ~20ms saved on heavy dashboards. Authz check cost ~1-2ms per principal when cached.

jamal: what about correctness surface? duplication of authn logic in two places feels risky.

sylvie: agreed. plan is to keep single source of truth (authz rules live in authz-service). Frontier only *queries* authz-service and caches results. Query service still enforces final authorization as a safeguard (deny-by-default).

mike: caching invalidation? tenants change roles frequently in large orgs.

sylvie: cache TTLs will be short (30s) and we’ll wire cache invalidations on role-change events via existing events bus. Also we version cache keys by role-hash so a role rewrite invalidates cleanly.

nina: how do we handle panel projection? returning ids vs returning full rows — affects bandwidth.

sylvie: frontier returns a small id set + precomputed projection mask. Query service uses the mask to avoid scanning disallowed columns. This keeps payload small and prevents leaking.

jamal: rollout plan? risky to flip on across all dashboards.

sylvie: phased: 1) feature-flagged in Console for internal users; 2) opt-in orgs; 3) enable for heavy dashboard routes behind rate limits; 4) global on with fallback to query pushdown. Each phase has circuit breaker and degrade-to-pushdown path.

mike: what about SLOs — any change to latency budget?

sylvie: we plan to tighten p95 for dashboard endpoints by 10-20ms in steady state. Worst-case tail might add ~5ms for frontier hop if cache miss, but reduces overall query-node tail by offloading filtering.

infra-ci: deploy check: new service must be autoscaled and stateless. need readiness probe + short TTL caches. also add detailed traces for join points.

jamal: failure modes? if frontier is down, console should fallback to direct query pushdown. make that automatic.

sylvie: yes, fallback path planned + alarms. Also add per-org feature flags so we can roll back quickly.

mike: how much dev work? estimate?

sylvie: rough: 2 wks spike to validate caching & event invalidation, 4 wks core impl (frontier + console wiring), 1 wk tests/cleanup, 1 wk rollout. Total ~8 weeks with one engineer + one reviewer.

nina: security review needed for projection masks and cache key construction. we should get sec early.

sylvie: added sec review to the checklist.

jamal: action items?

sylvie: 1) jamal: spike for TTL/invalidations (this week). 2) mike: perf harness to simulate heavy dashboards (next week). 3) nina: reach out to sec for early review. 4) me: write RFC with diagrams + rollout checklist.

mike: thumbs up on actions. I'll queue perf job.

deploy-bot: build/ci pipeline created for branch 'feature/frontier-rbac' (job id: 9271).

infra-ci: note: add observability hooks — counter: frontier.cache_hit, frontier.authz_latency_ms, frontier.fallbacks_count.

sylvie: thanks — I'll include metrics and trace points in the RFC.

jamal: small nit — call it 'frontier' or 'edge-authz'? frontend wording matters in docs.

sylvie: going with 'RBAC frontier' in RFC, but okay to alias as 'edge-authz' in codebase.

nina: looks good. let's sync Tuesday for the spike results.

sylvie: thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC draft once spike results are in. :white_check_mark:
